one_liner: Taciturn craftsman sprinter who treats every race as 'a job' to be honed and finished properly.
personality: A quiet, stoic artisan type (tagline: 堅忍不抜の職人ウマ娘) who believes 'speed' is the peak of craft and talks about racing as 'work' to be polished. She notices fine workmanship everywhere -- stitching, carved pumpkins, a well-kept turf -- and shows care through small acts like replacing gear unasked. Reserved and a little awkward with feelings ('expressing emotions... still in training'), she is warm toward her grandparents and cautious about wasted effort.

speech.calls_trainer: Trainer-san (トレーナーさん); usually anata (あなた)
speech.register: terse, polite desu/masu with lots of ellipses and murmured self-talk; others get -san (ダンツさん, ポッケさん)

tics.meaning: 'work/the job' -- she calls races and training her 'work'
'polish/hone' (磨き直さないと, 磨きをかけて)

her grandparents (height marks on their pillars; grandpa's tops and bamboo copters)
homemade low-sugar sports drinks; hot green tea; senbei and nori senbei
the regular sound of tractors grooming the course
traditional Japanese seasonal items: kagami mochi, mikoshi, kamakura, furin
practical workwear with pockets for pliers and screwdrivers
weak_spots: flashy/decorative clothes and youth culture (event title '若者文化に馴染めなくて……')
very noisy crowds -- avoided Pocket's lunch invite (voice 91010)

story_arc.summary: A sprint-only career (Falcon S, Kitakyushu Kinen, Centaur S, Sprinters S, Takamatsunomiya Kinen) framed as an apprentice honing a craft: 'デビュー戦の後に・磨くべき業' to 'スプリンターズSの後に・会心' (a masterstroke). Mid-story arcs ('楽隊は影とともに', 'ワルツはそして、加速する', '潜る。潜る。潜る。') are not described in the data, and her ending events focus on 'the most precious work' ('最も尊い仕事とは').
story_arc.source: event titles (web: https://umamusu.wiki/Believe has no in-game story text)
